stories.title: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been a singular figure in the development of the AI industry, which suddenly has to survive without him.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI
sources.text: Michael Dell described Jensen Huang as a "visionary of the AI age." Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges said a photo with the Nvidia CEO produced more media coverage for his company than its iPhone launch. During the keynote of his annual Dreamforce conference, Salesforce's Marc Benioff said, "Jensen, we're all following you, bro," as the two paced through the audience. Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation His fame extended way beyond tech. In May, Huang joined President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to China to meet with President Xi Jinping . Three months later, Huang gathered six of the biggest names at the Nasdaq to announce on CNBC a proposed $500 billion artificial intelligence buildout plan, cementing his central role at the intersection of Wall Street and Silicon Valley. As Nvidia became the first company to rip past a $5 trillion market cap, bending the laws of physics with its advanced graphics processing units and pushing the AI boom to seemingly endless bounds, the now 63-year-old Huang, clad in a black leather jacket, traversed the globe as the face of the brand powering the next industrial revolution. Over the past week it all came crashing down. Following two reported extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with an employee — Huang is leaving the company he co-founded 33 years ago in crisis, and thrusting the AI market into chaos. The board is now left to pick a successor for a company that's been run by a singular figure with no second-in-command. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Harvey Jones has been appointed chairman. Nvidia has not responded to multiple requests for comment. "How companies handle a crisis determines their future," former Cisco CEO John Chambers, now a startup investor, told CNBC's " Fast Money " on Wednesday. "How they handle this will determine if they're a great company and a great leadership team beyond one person." It had been a tumultuous stretch for Nvidia, even before the Huang saga led the board to launch an investigation of the CEO's behavior and the potential national security implications. The stock is on pace for its sixth straight weekly drop, which would be the longest losing streak since 2012. That includes a 9% slump last week after the midterm elections resulted in sweeping Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress, and the passage of dozens of ballot measures that could slow the buildout of new data centers. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday, and expectations remain high, with analysts projecting 92% year-over-year revenue growth to $109.2 billion, according to LSEG. That's up 18-fold from the same quarter in 2022, just before OpenAI launched ChatGPT and kicked off the generative AI era. It's a historic level of growth for any business, and particularly notable for a company that spent most of its first few decades as a niche technology provider for video games. Huang founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, he and other executives saw an opportunity to put GPUs to work for computationally intense projects. That technology eventually turned Nvidia into the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense. In the process, Huang became the ultimate decider, choosing how, when and where GPUs get allocated. The biggest buyers were the hyperscalers — Amazon, Google , Meta and Microsoft — which needed the chips to build their own AI services and make them available to cloud customers. OpenAI , meanwhile, was snapping up GPUs for its powerful models and consumer apps. To expand his customer base, Huang designated compute capacity to a number of so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius , putting equity into the companies and helping them build big businesses around renting out GPUs. Oracle gobbled up billions of dollars worth of GPUs, going heavily into debt in the process. Elon Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX , did the same to build its Grok model, before eventually starting to rent out excess capacity to Anthropic and Google. Huang wanted the world standardizing on Nvidia. Last year he demanded that Oracle buy additional Nvidia networking hardware if it wanted allocation to its state-of-the-art Grace Blackwell chips, said two people familiar with the deal who asked not to be named because the negotiations were private. In August, Nvidia said it will provide up to $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio that could be the largest of its kind in the world. "He created the product that started the industry," said Chris Miglino, CEO of neocloud Axe Compute . " Without his leadership we may be many years behind where we are today with AI chip technology, which is the driving force behind the neocloud market." When it comes to investing cash in fledgling startups, Huang is known to host entrepreneurs at Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters. While there could be 30 Nvidia employees in the room for the pitch meeting, only Huang asks questions, according to people with knowledge of the matter, who requested anonymity because they're not authorized to speak publicly about it. One source told CNBC that key aspects of project finance are so reliant on Huang's sign-off that, when he travels, those involved in the deal are forced to wait for his plane to land before learning if they can go forward or if terms have to be renegotiated. Huang's ambitions extended well beyond the U.S. He wanted to be a force in China, which became a difficult market for Nvidia during the Biden administration and was virtually off-limits after Trump implemented strict export controls in his second term. Huang's aggressive pursuit of China may have been his undoing. sources.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was the Jenga piece to a towering multi-trillion AI industry. Will his exit set off a chain reaction?
sources.text: Tech industry insiders awoke Thursday morning with an unfamiliar, and somewhat alarming notion to contemplate: life without Jensen Huang. Huang’s abrupt resignation as CEO leaves one of the world’s most valuable companies without the leader who has steered it for the past 33 years; the person who almost singlehandedly transformed Nvidia from a small maker of video game graphics chips into the driving force of the AI boom. “NVIDIA’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom,” Stephanie Balaouras, Forrester’s VP, group research director, told Fortune . The importance of Nvidia, and of Huang, to the AI industry extends well beyond the company’s own P&L statement. In addition to being the leading maker of the GPU chips powering AI services like ChatGPT and Claude, Nvidia has become the AI industry’s “central bank” financing scores of other companies. And then there’s Huang’s unique standing as AI’s senior statesman and cheerleader on everything from AI regulation to industrial policy. Whether the AI industry turns out to have lost its most famous champion with the ignominious exit of Huang and his famous black leather coat, or a more crucial, Jenga-like piece may be the most important economic question to be answered in the coming weeks and months. “Obviously Nvidia is more than Jensen Huang, but he kind of championed a whole range of investments,” a VC investor focused on early-stage companies told Fortune . “There is a question around whether the pace of investment in AI and the size of the amounts of capital going into companies can be continued. Because by any stretch of the imagination, it’s been quite extreme,” the investor said. In the immediate aftermath of the news, the stock market appears to be keeping its composure. While shares of Nvidia were down 6.3% in midday trading on Thursday, and certain AI-linked stocks took a hit, the broader market reaction was relatively muted, with the Nasdaq down only 95 points. But with spending on AI and data centers so important to the broader U.S. economy, the extent of the potential fallout from the Nvidia shakeup is difficult to overstate. Looming largest on the horizon is Anthropic’s widely anticipated initial public offering , scheduled to occur next week. The Anthropic IPO (along with OpenAI’s IPO expected in 2027) represent make-or-break moments for the AI industry—closely watched events that will serve as proxies for the health, and momentum, of the AI business. If nothing else, one startup founder told Fortune , the Nvidia drama raises the stakes for Anthropic’s upcoming IPO: “If the Anthropic IPO doesn’t go well and if the OpenAI IPO [down the line] doesn’t go well, there’s a question of: Is there a path to profitability for any players in the AI space?” Antropic is seeking to raise upwards of $60 billion in the offering slated for November 18, giving the five-year old AI company a valuation that could exceed $1.4 trillion when it makes its expected Wall Street debut next week. Karl Alomar, a partner at venture firm M13, argued that investors will recognize the strength in Anthropic’s business, regardless of the Nvidia shakeup. “From where I stand, Anthropic is still in as good, as strong and as good a position as it was before this news came out,” Alomar said. “I’m not sure it’ll have a massive impact on them. Anthropic’s numbers are fantastic, and they’ve clearly shown that they have excess capacity for what they need,” he said. Anthropic’s business prospects are closely intertwined with those of the cloud providers, which provide the data centers and compute capacity to train and run AI models like Claude. (According to Anthropic’s S-1 filing, it has roughly $900 billion in compute spending commitments over the next several decades.) While the tech giants like Alphabet , Amazon , and Microsoft have the wherewithal to ride out whatever turbulence is caused by the changes at Nvidia, the situation may be trickier for the smaller “neo-cloud” companies —many financed by Nvidia—that buy Nvidia chips in bulk and rent out the computing power. Huang has championed these neo-cloud companies because it was good for business and the company’s influence, Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners and one of the few on Wall Street with a sell rating on Nvidia’s stock. “He’d rather have 300 small customers who are dependent on him than three massive ones who you can’t negotiate with,” he said. With Nvidia CFO Coleen Kress now serving as interim CEO, the company’s attitude towards neo-clouds could shift. According to a report in The Information on Thursday, Kress has occasionally pushed back against Huang’s deals in the AI ecosystem, including a deal to backstop $250 billion in credit for an OpenAI datacenter project. The “Nvidia money train” that has kept parts of the market that propped up could come to an end, said one venture capital partner invested in numerous AI startups. “ The idea that they could count on Nvidia for future financing is unlikely.” Shares of CoreWeave one of the leading neocloud providers were down 7.5% on Thursday, while Nebius Group, another neo-cloud company which gave a lighter-than-expected sales forecast during its quarterly earnings on Thursday, were down 18%. Investors are likely to look harder at the numbers Huang used to justify the complex web of investments. Jason Schloetzer, an associate professor at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business, expects investors and policymakers alike may start re-examining “Jensen math.” U.S. policy towards data centers could also come in for harsher treatment, particularly after last week’s midterm elections in which voters overwhelmingly registered their opposition to having the facilities built in their communities. Huang gave much of the industry credibility, even amid the backlash to datacenters. He was well-liked and not seen as a polarizing political figure, said Goldberg, of Seaport Research. sources.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
sources.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal. In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China . She’s also an executive of a Singapore-based neocloud that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels. Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company. Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies. It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation. Republican committee chairs are already summoning him to testify in closed-door sessions about the security ramifications. Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill? No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump. Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September? Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters. Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it. In other words, he is a billionaire close to Trump. He was — until Thursday — the face of AI and data centers (also a deeply unpopular political topic with voters), and he has publicly admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Even though he’s no longer CEO, that seems too juicy a target for Democrats to ignore. Beyond whatever may be coming, Huang’s influence has been lost right when he was using it to push the tech industry in a number of directions. These areas have now lost their biggest champion. Huang has been the biggest, loudest advocate for open-weight AI models in the tech industry and among government policymakers. Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more. It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.) In July, when Anthropic and OpenAI were reportedly urging the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organized a letter of support for open-weight models generally (if not Chinese models specifically), signed by hundreds of tech companies. Open-weight models give enterprises choice in the market and reduce costs. Without Huang, the next biggest advocate for them is perhaps Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, but he’s not out there organizing the industry to speak up. Both OpenAI and Anthropic revealed incident after incident this year as their AI agents hacked into others’ networks or performed other misdeeds. Huang loudly proclaimed the AI industry still didn’t need regulation and would deal with safety itself. As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again. Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents. Naturally, this effort hasn’t instantly solved the problem , and now the top spokesperson for self-regulation via technology solutions is out of his position of influence. Huang has also been among the loudest voices insisting that AI is an engineered system that creates products, and so can be controlled like any other engineered system. This viewpoint counters the AI doomers and even the big AI labs themselves, which sometimes position their models as on the verge of consciousness (Anthropic) or as alien minds (OpenAI) . While Huang deals with the fallout of his actions, the loudest voice of this counter-narrative is, for the foreseeable future, silenced. Huang also just convinced a long list of PC makers to buy into his long-time dream of providing CPUs (the main processor chips) for them. In this age, when most Americans have not experienced AI beyond a chatbot, he orchestrated a new line of high-end AI PCs geared for running agents locally. These new PCs are due out this holiday season, and they may sell well for their intended targets: creators, developers, and others already savvy with agents. But now that Huang has become a meme for cheating on his wife with an alleged spy, he’s perhaps not the best choice to help market these devices as a cool alternative to the Mac mini. Huang demolished his reputation right as bond underwriters (lenders) and bond buyers are pretty much over AI build-out-related debt. Of roughly $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year, nearly half were rated high-risk “junk,” Forbes reports. Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing. Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips. By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported. In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported . Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up. sources.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
sources.text: A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here. A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here. I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi. Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out. Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents ), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad : business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.” Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46. Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China . But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.” Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office a month ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished . The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address. Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing . The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun! Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON , according to Bloomberg . Liang and Super Micro have not been charged. But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists , and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times. The question, of course, is how high this all goes Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point , actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming. More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed , which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “ more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him . The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom . This is what gangster tech regulation looks like. I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know? Come January, Elizabeth Warren will be able to send subpoenas in her role as the chair of the Senate Banking Committee. And wouldn’t you know, she seems to be pretty interested . Democrats will control both the House and the Senate. Their voters have given them a mandate to root out corruption. And boy howdy, does Nvidia look like a sittin

sources.title: Ex-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is set to testify before Congress this month
sources.text: House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast said the hearing will take place before Thanksgiving. Jensen Huang might have stepped down from his roles at the top of NVIDIA, but he won't be sliding out of the spotlight just yet. The company's former CEO and president is set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, according to House representatives. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said Huang agreed to testify on Wednesday — hours before NVIDIA announced his resignation with immediate effect — after lawmakers threatened him with a subpoena. It appears the hearing will take place behind closed doors (which is unfortunate, because that's likely to be some spicy testimony). However, Mast expects it to be filmed and transcribed, according to Bloomberg . The House's Intelligence and China-focused committees will join the Foreign Affairs cohort for the hearing. "Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but NVIDIA is a very important company to the United States of America," Mast said. "I don't want to see anything hurt in NVIDIA, but he has some very serious questions to answer." NVIDIA has been in turmoil after it emerged over the weekend that the company was investigating Huang over an affair to which he admitted, allegedly with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating the situation as well. On Wednesday, it was reported that Huang had another affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. The company's board met later that day to determine Huang's future. Colette Kress, NVIDIA's executive vice president and chief financial officer, is stepping in as interim CEO while the company seeks a permanent successor. Meanwhile, the Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Alice Huang , the alleged spy, to determine whether entities associated with her were involved in attempts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China. The DoJ is also said to be taking the lead in an investigation into her former company, the Singapore-based Megaspeed International, over alleged smuggling of US-made chips into China in defiance of export restrictions. The company said it would cooperate with the probe . Officials in Singapore opened an investigation into Alice Huang, Megaspeed and associated individuals last year. The Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement on Thursday that she was barred from re-entering the country after police determined she knowingly offered up inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed. However, they "concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated." The investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is ongoing.

sources.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
sources.text: The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models. Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community. Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion . Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source , whatever happens next. Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology. Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development. Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab. Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem. Earlier this year, Huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China. The impetus for that letter was Washington’s debate over how the U.S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections. That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons. Without Huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes. Huang’s exit could also strengthen the arguments of those in Washington who are arguing for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies, particularly as the scandal surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and alleged spy, puts renewed scrutiny on his efforts to loosen chip export controls. Restrictions on open-weight models from China could kneecap competition for American companies, the most powerful of which have kept their models closed. Still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project Huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy. As some of Nvidia’s biggest customers, including Google and OpenAI, develop their own chips, Nvidia has an incentive to cultivate a much broader ecosystem of AI developers and customers. More players training, fine-tuning, and running models mean more GPUs sold, and less dependence on a handful of frontier labs. Huang may be gone, but Nvidia still needs an open AI ecosystem. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority. TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence. Rebecca Bellan is a senior reporter at TechCrunch where she covers the business, policy, and emerging trends shaping artificial intelligence. Her work has also appeared in Forbes, Bloomberg, The Atlantic, The Daily Beast, and other publications. sources.title: NVIDIA prepara demissão de Jensen Huang após segundo caso de traição
sources.text: Por Raphael Giannotti | 12/11/2026 às 11:34 Se você é PC gamer, viu Jensen Huang, fundador e único CEO da história da NVIDIA, subir ao palco e apresentar novas placas de vídeo por anos. Isso pode mudar daqui pra frente, já que o conselho administrativo da empresa está discutindo a demissão do executivo agora após outro caso extraconjugal vir à tona . Segundo o The Wall Street Journal, a diretoria se prepara para destituir o líder que comanda a gigante dos semicondutores há 33 anos, em uma reunião decisiva que pode selar a primeira troca de comando desde a fundação da companhia em 1993. O estopim para a mudança drástica foi uma reportagem do The New York Times revelando que Huang manteve um relacionamento com Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente da divisão de saúde da própria NVIDIA e sua subordinada direta . O caso se soma ao escândalo recente envolvendo a empresária e executiva Alice Huang , suspeita de atuar como agente da inteligência chinesa. Essa crise de governança e segurança nacional já fez as ações da fabricante despencarem 20% na bolsa de valores desde o início das revelações. De acordo com relatos de funcionários citados pela imprensa norte-americana, Huang e Powell foram vistos trocando carinhos em um hotel em San Jose, na Califórnia, durante a conferência GTC em março . Embora o código de conduta da NVIDIA não proíba expressamente todos os relacionamentos entre gestores e subordinados, as normas internas exigem que potenciais conflitos de interesse sejam reportados ao departamento jurídico. Além disso, trata-se de uma quebra de aliança matrimonial. Para conduzir a apuração independente, o conselho contratou o escritório de advocacia Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Caso a demissão de Huang se confirme, a empresa enfrentará um vácuo inédito de liderança: como o executivo mantém uma estrutura administrativa horizontal onde dezenas de vice-presidentes respondem diretamente a ele, não há um sucessor natural óbvio. Enquanto isso, os trabalhos dentro da gigante seguem, já que os data centers não podem parar. Para os gamers, tem sobrado cada vez menos. Parceiras da NVIDIA já até afirmaram que a empresa tem interrompido o fornecimento de chips para a fabricação de placas de vídeo GeForce RTX .

sources.title: Jensen Huang, executivo que deu protagonismo à IA, renuncia ao comando da Nvidia após escândalo extraconjugal e de espionagem
sources.text: O Conselho de Administração da Nvidia anunciou nesta quinta-feira (12) que Jensen Huang renunciou aos cargos de presidente, diretor-executivo e membro do conselho da empresa. A decisão tem efeito imediato. O fundador da Nvidia admitiu ter sido infiel à esposa após a revelação de um relacionamento com Alice Huang, suspeita de espionar para o governo da China. Apesar do sobrenome em comum, ela não tem parentesco com Jensen Huang. As ações da Nvidia desabaram mais de 24% em 30 dias. A empresa perdeu US$ 1,081 trilhão (cerca de R$ 6,1 trilhões) em valor de mercado entre 29 de outubro e 10 de novembro, segundo levantamento da Elos Ayta. No domingo (8), a companhia abriu uma investigação independente para apurar se ele foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência de outro país. Nesta quarta (11), o jornal New York Times revelou que Jensen também teve outro caso extraconjugal, desta vez com Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente da área de saúde da Nvidia. Em comunicado, a Nvidia informou que Colette Kress, atual vice-presidente executiva e diretora financeira, assumirá temporariamente o comando da empresa. Segundo a empresa, Kress teve um papel fundamental no crescimento da Nvidia à frente da área financeira. Antes de ingressar na companhia, ela acumulou quase 25 anos de experiência em cargos financeiros em empresas de tecnologia, incluindo Cisco e Microsoft. Comunicado da Nvidia sobre afastamento de Jensen Huang “O Conselho de Administração da NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) anunciou hoje que Jensen Huang renunciou aos cargos de Presidente, Diretor Executivo e membro do Conselho, com efeito imediato. Colette Kress, atual Vice-Presidente Executiva e Diretora Financeira da NVIDIA, concordou em atuar como Diretora Executiva Interina. Kress continuará atuando como Vice-Presidente Executivo e Diretor Financeiro enquanto atua como Diretor Executivo Interino até que um sucessor permanente seja nomeado. O Conselho está iniciando uma busca por um Diretor Executivo permanente e considerará candidatos internos e externos. Kress atua como Vice-Presidente Executivo e Diretor Financeiro da NVIDIA desde que ingressou na empresa em setembro de 2013. Durante seu mandato, ela liderou a organização financeira da empresa e desempenhou um papel fundamental no crescimento e evolução da NVIDIA. Antes de ingressar na NVIDIA, Kress passou quase 25 anos em cargos financeiros em empresas líderes de tecnologia, incluindo Cisco e Microsoft. O Conselho de Administração nomeou Harvey C. Jones como seu primeiro Presidente do Conselho. O Sr. Jones é empreendedor, executivo de tecnologia e investidor ativo de capital de risco há mais de 30 anos, incluindo atuando como Diretor Executivo e Presidente Executivo da Synopsys. “Colette ajudou a conduzir a NVIDIA durante um período de crescimento extraordinário e possui profundo entendimento do nosso negócio, clientes, operações e posição financeira”, disse Harvey Jones, presidente do Conselho de Administração da NVIDIA. “Ela conta com o apoio de uma equipe de liderança experiente que tem sido fundamental na execução da estratégia da NVIDIA e no avanço de seu roteiro tecnológico. O Conselho tem total confiança em Colette e na equipe de liderança, e esperamos que as operações da empresa, compromissos com clientes e roteiro de produto continuem sem interrupções.” “A força da NVIDIA sempre veio de suas equipes e, junto com nossa equipe de liderança, estou comprometido em construir sobre a extraordinária base que Jensen criou nos últimos 33 anos”, disse Colette Kress, CEO interina e CFO da NVIDIA. “Continuaremos avançando no trabalho que tornou a NVIDIA líder em computação acelerada e IA, e executaremos as oportunidades que virão. Nosso foco permanece em servir nossos clientes, parceiros, desenvolvedores e acionistas.” As contribuições de Jensen para a NVIDIA são profundas. A NVIDIA é uma das empresas de tecnologia mais influentes do mundo. O Conselho e a empresa agradecem a Jensen por suas contribuições imensuráveis para a empresa e para a indústria. A NVIDIA divulgará seus resultados financeiros do terceiro trimestre fiscal de 2027 na terça-feira, 17 de novembro, por volta das 13h20 PT, conforme previsto anteriormente, seguido pela teleconferência de resultados às 14h PT.”

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: Saída de Jensen Huang abala Nvidia e pode redefinir o futuro da inteligência
sources.text: A renúncia de Jensen Huang ao comando da Nvidia abre uma incerteza que vai além da sucessão na fabricante de chips: a continuidade das relações comerciais e financeiras que ajudam a sustentar a expansão da inteligência artificial. O executivo tinha papel central na articulação de investimentos entre empresas do setor. A mudança ocorre em um momento em que fabricantes de semicondutores , provedores de nuvem e desenvolvedores de IA dependem de grandes compromissos financeiros para ampliar a infraestrutura necessária ao treinamento e à operação de modelos. A influência da Nvidia no mercado não se limita à venda de processadores. A empresa também participa de um ecossistema de investimentos e acordos com companhias que precisam de capacidade computacional para desenvolver serviços de inteligência artificial . Nesse arranjo, provedores de nuvem e laboratórios de IA dependem de infraestrutura equipada com chips da fabricante, enquanto os investimentos e compromissos comerciais ajudam a viabilizar novas instalações. Huang teve participação direta na construção dessas relações. Sua atuação envolvia não apenas a estratégia tecnológica da Nvidia, mas também a articulação com parceiros e clientes que impulsionam a demanda por seus produtos. A saída do executivo, portanto, levanta dúvidas sobre a capacidade da companhia de manter esse ritmo de coordenação. O desafio não está necessariamente no desenvolvimento dos próximos chips . A Nvidia conta com equipes técnicas e um planejamento de produtos que não dependem exclusivamente de seu fundador. A questão é como a empresa manterá a rede de acordos, investimentos e operações que conecta diferentes participantes do mercado de IA. Um dos pontos de atenção é o chamado financiamento circular. O modelo ocorre quando empresas que fornecem tecnologia ou infraestrutura também investem em clientes ou oferecem garantias que ajudam a financiar compras de seus próprios produtos e serviços. Esse tipo de relação pode acelerar a construção de data centers e a expansão da capacidade computacional. Ao mesmo tempo, cria vínculos financeiros entre empresas que dependem umas das outras para manter seus planos de crescimento. Se compromissos forem revistos ou novos investimentos demorarem a sair, os efeitos podem alcançar diferentes partes da cadeia. Anúncios e acordos envolvendo empresas como OpenAI , CoreWeave e Anthropic ilustram a dimensão dos recursos mobilizados para ampliar a infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. A continuidade desses projetos depende de financiamento, disponibilidade de equipamentos e confiança na demanda futura. A renúncia de Huang não significa que esses compromissos serão interrompidos. Mas sua saída acrescenta uma variável à avaliação dos investidores: quem assumirá a articulação de negócios em um setor no qual decisões de investimento de uma empresa podem influenciar os planos de várias outras? A reação inicial das ações mostrou a dimensão da preocupação dos investidores. Os papéis da Nvidia recuaram mais de 12% nas negociações iniciais desta quinta-feira (12), movimento que poderia retirar cerca de US$ 500 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 2,78 trilhões) de seu valor de mercado. AMD e Broadcom, por outro lado, registraram altas de 2% e 5%, respectivamente. A diretora financeira Colette Kress assumirá o comando interinamente, enquanto a empresa avalia candidatos internos e externos para a sucessão definitiva. A Nvidia também terá de demonstrar que consegue preservar sua estratégia comercial e os relacionamentos construídos por Huang. O desempenho financeiro recente oferece uma base operacional robusta: a companhia reportou US$ 96,2 bilhões (cerca de R$ 533,9 bilhões) em receita no último trimestre. Ainda assim, os próximos resultados, previstos para 17 de novembro, serão acompanhados não apenas pelos números de vendas, mas também por sinais sobre demanda, entregas e novos investimentos. O alcance da transição será medido, portanto, pela capacidade da Nvidia de manter sua posição na cadeia de infraestrutura da IA. Mais do que encontrar um novo CEO, a empresa precisa mostrar que o ecossistema de negócios construído durante a gestão de Huang pode continuar funcionando sem depender de sua presença direta. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? O que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang
sources.text: O dia 12 de novembro de 2026 ficará marcado no mundo da tecnologia como um dos mais improváveis e até mesmo mais importantes de sua história. Nesta quinta-feira, Jensen Huang, o CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, renunciou ao cargo após um escândalo de adultério e espionagem. As reações do mercado de tecnologia e Wall Street já eram esperadas. Somente nas últimas horas, as ações da companhia verde caíram mais de 13%. O próprio Huang saiu do seleto grupo das dez pessoas mais ricas do mundo nos últimos três dias ao perder quase US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 50 bilhões) de sua fortuna absurda, estimada em mais de R$ 700 bilhões. Por mais que a indústria de tecnologia e o segmento de IA possam enfrentar um período de incertezas, a expectativa é que esse mercado continue firme. No entanto, a pergunta que uma generosa parcela do público começa a fazer é: o que acontece com os gamers de computador? Além do gigantismo em IA, a Nvidia é dona da tradicional linha de placas de vídeo GeForce, que alimenta 72% dos computadores dos gamers, segundo dados da Steam. Jogar no PC e usar uma Nvidia GeForce se tornou basicamente um sinônimo para muitos, e agora impera o medo de que essa divisão esteja ameaçada. A Nvidia publicou uma nota recente que explica a renúncia de Jensen Huang como diretor da empresa. Interinamente, Colette Kress atuará como CEO da companhia até que a empresa e o Conselho encontrem um executivo (a) definitivo. Em outras palavras, as portas da Nvidia estão abertas e não há como prever integralmente quais mudanças serão implementadas na gigante. Mesmo assim, a curto e até médio prazo talvez seja seguro dizer que a divisão GeForce de placas de vídeo ficará intocada. É verdade que a Nvidia já direcionava seus esforços quase que totalmente para o segmento corporativo, mas isso não quer dizer que a empresa abandonará seu braço de gráficos e GPUs. Arthur Igreja, especialista em tecnologia e inovação, aponta que o estágio embrionário do momento impossibilita fazer previsões assertivas . No entanto, ele explica que é improvável a Nvidia simplesmente se livrar da linha gamer, afinal de contas, ninguém parece disposto a se livrar de uma divisão inteira assim. Uma coisa é ter foco, outra, completamente diferente, é abrir mão. Essa ainda é uma linha de receita importante para a Nvidia. O especialista salienta que em momentos de crise, como o atual, a companhia precisará reunir todas as suas linhas para maximizar o lucro. O fato de a divisão GeForce existir pode até mesmo ser um fator positivo para a companhia. Aliás, a nova CEO era diretora financeira da empresa, então ela deve saber da importância dessa série e pode evitar cortes desnecessários agora. Claro, isso não significa que os produtos GeForce ficarão intocados para sempre . Um futuro CEO pode entender que a linha gamer e de itens domésticos não faz sentido e focar toda a infraestrutura da empresa para o setor corporativo. Mesmo assim, isso seria um movimento brusco extremamente arriscado. Vale notar que o mundo do hardware doméstico contempla apenas três empresas: Nvidia, AMD e Intel. A AMD é a única com força para produzir amplamente CPUs e GPUs, e a Intel engatinha no cenário das placas de vídeo. Abrir mão da série GeForce seria entregar o mercado de bandeja para a AMD e ver a Intel ganhar terreno ao longo dos anos. Arthur Igreja também aponta que o movimento de saída de Jensen Huang da Nvidia também não deve ser motivo para reduzir a crise de componentes global. “A questão da demanda é um fator externo, exógeno. Ela depende muito mais das hyperscalers e do restante do mercado, além de fatores como um eventual aumento da regulação [...] Em última instância, a NVIDIA continua sendo uma fornecedora. Ela não representa o mercado como um todo e não controla a demanda”. Mesmo com sua atuação distante do segmento gamer, Colette Kress já mostrou em algumas oportunidades que entende o fenômeno. Durante uma conversa com analistas da JPMorgan na CES 2026, a executiva foi questionada sobre a ausência de novidades para o setor na feira e respondeu que “o negócio de games tem sido um sucesso estrondoso”. Aliás, a própria entrada de Kress na Nvidia em 2013 aconteceu por conta do setor de games. Ela entrou na companhia após seus filhos recomendarem a marca por conta dos bons produtos gamer que produzia. O TecMundo já possui um ótimo conteúdo que conta detalhadamente a história completa da Nvidia, mas é sempre bom relembrar como um gigante se ergue. Tudo começou em 1993, quando Curtis Priem, Christopher Malachowski e um jovem chamado Jensen Huang fundaram a Nvidia em Sunnyvale, na Califórnia. Engana-se quem pensa que a estrada até o sucesso da Nvidia foi pavimentada com ouro - ou melhor, silício. O primeiro chip comercial da companhia surgiu apenas em 1995, o NV1, mas foi em 1997 que as coisas realmente começaram a engrenar graças ao sucesso da linha Riva. Mas foi em outubro de 1999 que a linha GeForce deu seu passo inaugural com a GeForce 256. Jensen e seus amigos acreditavam que os computadores se tornaram uma plataforma multimídia e de jogos 3D. A chegada da GeForce 256 confirmou isso ao se tornar a primeira GPU como conhecemos hoje. De 1999 até 2026 tem muita história para contar. A Nvidia comprou rivais, como a 3dfx, desenvolveu o chip do primeiro Xbox, do PlayStation 3, fez com que os usuários pudessem usar várias placas de vídeo em um único PC e por aí vai. Lá em 2008 a companhia verde resolveu lançar uma placa chamada GTX 280. A partir de então, as GTX se tornaram as placas de vídeo definitivas para os jogadores, mesmo a rival AMD tendo adquirido a fabricante de GPUs ATI para rivalizar forças. Não tinha jeito, a Nvidia dominava esse segmento. Os anos passaram e uma década depois da introdução da GTX 280 a Nvidia resolveu revolucionar o mundo dos PCs de novo: entrou em cena a linha RTX. Esses produtos, que perduram até hoje, tinham o poder para calcular raios de luz em tempo real, o Ray Tracing, e isso possibilitou que os games ficassem exponencialmente

sources.title: Quién es Colette Kress, la nueva CEO temporal de Nvidia tras la dimisión de Jensen Huang por el escándalo de sus infidelidades
sources.text: La compañía de inteligencia artificial Nvidia ha cobrado especial protagonismo durante los últimos días tras conocerse los escándalos que envuelven a su ya antiguo CEO. Jensen Huang , quien ha ocupado el cargo hasta hace escasas horas, ha dimitido tras revelarse dos infidelidades . Una de ellas con una presunta espía china y otra con una subordinada directa. Debido a este escándalo, la junta directiva de la empresa evaluó su posible despido , pero que no ha tenido que llevarse a cabo, ya que Huang presentó su renuncia voluntaria. Esta crisis ha impactado severamente en el mercado. En las últimas cinco sesiones, la multinacional ha perdido cerca de 470.000 millones de dólares de capitalización, profundizando una caída que alcanza los 1,32 billones en un mes. En bolsa, Nvidia ha pasado de valer 5,52 billones de dólares a 4,19 billones , cediendo a Apple el primer puesto mundial. La sucesión plantea dudas operativas debido al modelo hiperpersonalista de Huang, quien fundó la empresa en 1993 y supervisaba directamente a sesenta ejecutivos sin haber designado un relevo claro. Ante este vacío en el liderazgo, el cargo de Huang lo ocupará, de manera temporal, la vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera de la compañía, Colette Kress, quien se incorporó al puesto en septiembre de 2013 , avalada por casi 25 años de experiencia en grandes firmas tecnológicas, según consta en la página web de Nvidia. Antes de su llegada, Kress trabajó tres años en Cisco como vicepresidenta sénior y directora financiera del grupo BTOF. En esa división asumió la responsabilidad sobre la estrategia financiera, la planificación, la generación de informes y el desarrollo de todos los segmentos operativos y de ingeniería. Su trayectoria previa incluye trece años en Microsoft , donde ejerció durante cuatro ejercicios como directora financiera de la división de Servidores y Herramientas , además de ocupar diversos puestos de responsabilidad vinculados a la planificación. Sus inicios profesionales se desarrollaron en el área financiera de Texas Instruments. En el ámbito académico, la nueva máxima responsable de la multinacional tecnológica es graduada en Finanzas por la Universidad de Arizona . Asimismo, completó su formación superior cursando un máster en Administración de Empresas (MBA) impartido por la Universidad Metodista del Sur. Además, Forbes situó a Kress en el puesto número 32 en el ranking 2026 America's Richest Self-Made Women Net Worth (mujeres que se hicieron ricas a sí mismas), con un patrimonio de 1.200 millones de dólares. Según Reuters , al cierre del mercado este miércoles, sus acciones en Nvidia estaban valoradas en aproximadamente 750 millones de dólares. sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Betting markets see a longtime Nvidia insider as the favorite to replace Jensen Huang, interim CEO Colette Kress is second
sources.text: Jensen Huang is out, and prediction market bettors are already putting money on who will take his place atop Nvidia . Trading in contracts on his successor picked up earlier this week on Kalshi and Polymarket, generating hundreds of thousands of dollars in trading volume. On Thursday, Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation and named finance chief Colette Kress interim CEO, adding that the board is searching for a permanent successor and will consider internal and external candidates. Kress, however, is not the favorite to take the top job. Instead, Nvidia VP and general manager of its high-performance computing division, Ian Buck, who has been at Nvidia since 2004, leads the field on Kalshi with 37% odds. Kress follows at 19%, ahead of Rene Haas, CEO of Arm Holdings, at 9%. Arm is a British chip designer that licenses its technology to Nvidia. Trading volume in the market has already surpassed $1.5 million. Polymarket’s market shows a similar lineup, with the same leading contenders drawing comparable odds and trading volume nearing $630,000. Madison Huang, Jensen Huang’s daughter and Nvidia’s senior director of product marketing, trails the leading contenders, with less than a 1% chance of succeeding him on Kalshi and roughly 2% on Polymarket. Prediction markets have been capitalizing on the turmoil at Nvidia since the company announced an investigation into Huang, who told its board he had an intimate relationship with a business executive reportedly identified by U.S. intelligence officials as a Chinese spy. The scrutiny intensified Wednesday, when reports surfaced alleging that Huang also had an extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee. Bettors are wagering on more than Nvidia’s next leader. One Polymarket contract generated more than $22.5 million in trading volume on when Huang would announce his departure. Another active Kalshi contract asks when Huang will testify before Congress and has drawn nearly $170,000 in trading volume. Traders put the odds of testimony before next July at 93%, compared with roughly 91% before January and 86% before December. The turmoil has also put Nvidia’s stock price in focus, with shares down roughly 5% Thursday morning at about $165. Traders on Kalshi are also betting on those price swings through perpetual futures contracts, taking positions on whether the price will rise or fall without owning shares. Those contracts recorded $111 million in trading volume over the past 24 hours.

sources.title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia — who is Colette Kress, his interim replacement?
sources.text: The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately. This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan . But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia. While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion? According to Nvidia’s website , Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. The California-based 59-year-old has a very limited social media presence — on Linkedin , she has commented some well wishes on former colleagues’ posts about their retirement. But as CFO, she’s been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company. According to Forbes’ list of America’s Richest Self-Made Women, Kress’ net worth is estimated to be about $1.2 billion. Her Forbes profile adds that she initially joined Nvidia in part because her two sons endorsed the company for its role in the video game industry, which it was best known for at the time. “Nvidias strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement . “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Nvidia is slated to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, when we will likely hear more from Kress about her plans for the company’s immediate future. sources.title: Jensen Huang dimite como CEO de NVIDIA tras el escándalo que sacude a la compañía: Colette Kress toma el mando
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. Jensen Huang, hasta ahora máximo responsable de NVIDIA, ha presentado su dimisión después de conocerse el escándalo de espionaje internacional que sacude a la compañía. Colette Kress, hasta ahora directora financiera, ha sido nombrada CEO interina mientras se busca un sustituto definitivo. Jensen Huang ha presentado su dimisión como CEO NVIDIA, con efecto inmediato . La compañía ha nombrado a Colette Kress, hasta ahora directora financiera, CEO interina mientras se busca a un sustituto definitivo. La salida del que ha sido el rostro más visible de la compañía llega en plena crisis reputacional por las informaciones sobre su vida personal y un posible caso de espionaje internacional. La dimisión de Huang supone un cambio histórico para NVIDIA, empresa que cofundó en 1993 y que ha dirigido durante más de tres décadas. Bajo su liderazgo, la multinacional ha pasado de ser uno de los principales fabricantes de tarjetas gráficas para videojuegos a convertirse en una pieza fundamental de la industria tecnológica gracias a sus procesadores para IA . Esta decisión llega después de varias informaciones sobre supuestas relaciones extramatrimoniales de Huang, una de ellas con Alice Huang, una empresaria china sobre la que las autoridades estadounidenses habrían mostrado sospechas por sus posibles vínculos con los servicios de inteligencia de Pekín . También han trascendido varios rumores sobre una posible segunda relación con Kimberly Powell, una directiva de NVIDIA que trabajaba bajo su supervisión. Todo esto habría llevado al consejo de administración de la empresa a abrir una investigación independiente para determinar si Huang había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia china para filtrar y robar información. La persona que asumirá provisionalmente las riendas de NVIDIA será Colette Kress , que lleva en la compañía desde septiembre de 2013 y hasta ahora ocupaba el puesto de vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera. Kress mantendrá también sus responsabilidades económicas mientras el consejo de administración busca un sustituto permanente. Antes de incorporarse a NVIDIA, la directiva acumuló cerca de 25 años de experiencia en departamentos financieros de grandes tecnológicas , entre ellas Cisco y Microsoft. El consejo considera que su experiencia de las cuentas, así como del funcionamiento interno de la compañía la convierten en una figura relevante para garantizar la continuidad del negocio durante esta transición. La compañía también ha anunciado el nombramiento de Harvey C. Jones como presidente del consejo de administración . Se trata de un movimiento significativo, ya que será el primer presidente de la junta directiva en la historia de NVIDIA. Jones lleva formando parte del consejo desde 1993 y cuenta con una larga trayectoria en el sector tecnológico y de la inversión. La dimisión de Jensen Huang llega en un momento especialmente delicado para el fabricante de chips . Su figura ha sido fundamental para construir la identidad de la compañía y establecer relaciones estratégicas con los principales proveedores de servicios en la nube, desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial y fabricantes de hardware. Además, el directivo había defendido públicamente la necesidad de mantener el acceso de NVIDIA al mercado chino , incluso en un contexto de restricciones estadounidenses a la exportación de semiconductores avanzados. Su salida también introduce incertidumbre sobre la posición que adoptará la compañía en este terreno. El consejo de administración de la compañía ha transmitido un mensaje de continuidad y confianza en el equipo directivo. La empresa asegura que sus operaciones y sus compromisos con los clientes no se verán afectados.
